appraisal_events.evidence: Stung by an innocent remark, Legrandin answers 'sans me donner la main et d'une voix rageuse et vulgaire que je ne lui soupçonnais pas'; the narrator concludes that 'tous ses mouvements convulsifs de colère ou d'amabilité étaient gouvernés par le désir d'avoir une bonne position' in the society he claims to disdain.
appraisal_events.explanation: Legrandin's vulgar, involuntary outburst betrays the very social anxiety and status-hunger his affected disdain for society was meant to conceal, deepening his established hypocrisy.

appraisal_events.evidence: The narrator describes her as if her title's 'duché' radiated around her, her eyes holding 'le ciel bleu d'une après-midi de France', and concludes 'la vie inconcevable que ce nom signifiait, ce corps la contenait bien'.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator's rapt description casts the duchesse as the living embodiment of the storied prestige of the Guermantes name, elevating her above the rest of the room.

status_effects.explanation: Legrandin is again exposed as a hypocrite whose pose of otherworldly disdain masks petty vanity and touchiness about his social standing.
His outburst confirms he is covertly dependent on the very social position he affects to scorn, weakening his claimed standing above society.
The narrator's admiring portrait presents her as uniquely embodying the mystique and prestige of her name.
